title: Audit Controls — ePHI Audit-Log Source Coverage & Periodic Activity Review
exclusions: Covers the audit-control mechanism itself — that every in-scope ePHI system is recording audit activity and that the activity is examined on a defined cadence. It does NOT adjudicate whether an individual access was appropriate (that is the access-anomaly and minimum-necessary UCs, e.g. UC-22.10.17 and UC-22.10.21), nor does it protect the log content's confidentiality/integrity (UC-22.35.2/22.35.3). Test, sandbox, and formally out-of-scope systems are excluded via the inventory lookup.
evidence: Saved search 'UC-22.10.59 — ePHI audit-control review' (scheduled monthly) writes a per-source coverage-and-activity record to the restricted audit_evidence index (6-year HIPAA retention); the companion dashboard 'Audit controls — ePHI source coverage' provides the timestamped operating-effectiveness evidence an auditor reviews for §164.312(b).

compliance.assurance_rationale: §164.312(b) requires mechanisms that both RECORD and EXAMINE activity in systems that contain ePHI. This UC is that mechanism end-to-end: it reconciles the in-scope ePHI system inventory against live audit telemetry to prove every system is recording (silent sources surface as an explicit GAP row), and it produces the periodic per-source activity-volume review that constitutes the examination. Splunk is the sole-sufficient control here — the audit-control standard is satisfied by operating this review — so the grade is full rather than partial.
compliance.controlObjective: Proves the covered entity operates audit controls that record and examine activity across every in-scope ePHI system, with silent audit sources flagged for follow-up.
compliance.evidenceArtifact: Saved search 'UC-22.10.59' over the ePHI audit sources (epic:audit, mssql:audit, WinEventLog:Security) reconciled against ephi_audit_sources.csv, archived monthly to the restricted audit_evidence index (6-year retention) with a coverage_status column an auditor can read directly.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Disable or stop forwarding for one in-scope ePHI audit source listed in ephi_audit_sources.csv (e.g. pause the Epic audit feed) for the duration of the review window. On the next scheduled run the source appears with audit_events=0 and coverage_status='GAP - expected ePHI audit source silent in review window', and the row routes to the audit_evidence index for follow-up.
controlTest.negativeScenario: When every in-scope ePHI source in the inventory is forwarding normally, all rows show audit_events greater than zero and coverage_status='recording', no GAP rows are produced, and the review record is archived as clean evidence of audit-control operation.

dataSources: `index=epic` `sourcetype=epic:audit`, `index=mssql` `sourcetype=mssql:audit`, `index=windows` `sourcetype=WinEventLog:Security` — the in-scope ePHI audit feeds; reconciled against inventory lookup `ephi_audit_sources.csv` (`sourcetype`, `system_name`, `ephi_owner`).
app: Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud Platform (native; no premium app required). Consumes audit feeds onboarded by the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742) plus the Epic and Microsoft SQL Server audit TAs (Splunkbase)
spl:
| tstats count as audit_events, dc(host) as reporting_hosts, latest(_time) as last_event where (index=epic sourcetype="epic:audit") OR (index=mssql sourcetype="mssql:audit") OR (index=windows sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security") earliest=-30d by sourcetype
| append [| inputlookup ephi_audit_sources.csv | eval audit_events=0]
| stats max(audit_events) as audit_events, max(reporting_hosts) as reporting_hosts, max(last_event) as last_event, values(system_name) as system_name, values(ephi_owner) as ephi_owner by sourcetype
| eval system_name=coalesce(system_name, sourcetype)
| eval coverage_status=if(audit_events>0, "recording", "GAP - expected ePHI audit source silent in review window")
| eval last_event=if(audit_events>0, strftime(last_event, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "never")
| eval reviewed_at=strftime(now(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
| table system_name, ephi_owner, sourcetype, audit_events, reporting_hosts, last_event, coverage_status, reviewed_at
| sort coverage_status, - audit_events
description: Operates the HIPAA audit-control mechanism for ePHI: it reconciles the authoritative inventory of in-scope ePHI systems against live audit telemetry, proving each system is recording (any expected source with no events in the review window is surfaced as an explicit GAP), and summarises the activity volume examined per source — the periodic examination the rule requires.
value: Turns §164.312(b) from an assertion ('we have audit logging') into replayable, timestamped evidence ('here is every in-scope ePHI system, its activity volume this period, and proof none went silent'). Gives the privacy and security office a single auditor-ready review record and catches the most damaging audit-control failure — a source that quietly stopped logging — before an assessor or incident does.
implementation: (1) Maintain ephi_audit_sources.csv (sourcetype, system_name, ephi_owner) as the version-controlled inventory of in-scope ePHI audit feeds; (2) schedule monthly to match the documented examination cadence; (3) route the result to the restricted audit_evidence index and email the per-source review to each ephi_owner; (4) open a ticket for any GAP row. Indexes required: `index=epic`, `index=mssql`, `index=windows`; Sourcetypes: `sourcetype=epic:audit`, `sourcetype=mssql:audit`, `sourcetype=WinEventLog:Security`; Lookups: `ephi_audit_sources.csv`.
visualization: Table (system, owner, sourcetype, audit_events, coverage_status) with GAP rows highlighted; single-value '% of in-scope ePHI sources recording'; time chart of audit_events per source over the review window. Key fields: `system_name`, `audit_events`, `coverage_status`.

references.title: 45 CFR §164.312 — HIPAA Security Rule: Technical safeguards
MITRE ATT&CK — T1562.008 Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Planned source decommissioning** — A system intentionally retired or migrated will show as a GAP until removed from ephi_audit_sources.csv; keep the inventory current as part of change management.

2. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Patching or upgrade windows can legitimately pause a source's audit feed; tag the source in a maintenance lookup so the GAP is annotated rather than treated as a finding.

3. **Low-activity systems** — A genuinely low-traffic ePHI system may report few events in a short window; the monthly cadence and the inventory-driven GAP logic (zero vs. non-zero) avoid flagging low-but-nonzero activity.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain the ephi_audit_sources.csv inventory and an optional maintenance_windows.csv; rows whose source is within an approved maintenance window are annotated, and decommissioned systems are removed from the inventory so they no longer count toward coverage.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Enterprise ≥9.2 or Splunk Cloud (current). No premium app is required — this control is platform-native and reads the audit feeds other ePHI UCs already onboard.
• **Audit feeds onboarded**: The in-scope ePHI systems must already be forwarding audit logs into Splunk — Epic Hyperspace audit (`epic:audit`), Microsoft SQL audit (`mssql:audit`), and Windows Security (`WinEventLog:Security`) are the reference set; add the sourcetypes for any other ePHI system in scope.
• **Inventory lookup**: `ephi_audit_sources.csv` must exist on the search tier with columns `sourcetype, system_name, ephi_owner`, one row per in-scope ePHI audit source. This file is the authoritative scope statement for the control — only sources listed here are expected to be recording, so its accuracy is the control's foundation. Version it in source control and review it whenever an ePHI system is added or retired.
• **Indexes**: `epic`, `mssql`, and `windows` must exist with retention meeting the HIPAA 6-year minimum (`frozenTimePeriodInSecs >= 189216000`) and a provisioned archive tier.
• **Regulatory mapping**: This control evidences `§164.312(b)` (Audit controls). Every result record carries `coverage_status` and `reviewed_at` so downstream consumers can read the audit-control operating evidence directly.

## Step 1 — Build and own the ePHI audit-source inventory

The control can only prove completeness if it knows what *should* be reporting. Populate `ephi_audit_sources.csv` from the system inventory the Privacy/Security Officer maintains — every application, database, and OS audit feed that records access to ePHI. A minimum row is `sourcetype, system_name, ephi_owner`; add `index` or `environment` columns if you need to scope further. Assign a named owner per source so GAP follow-up has an accountable recipient. Treat changes to this file as change-controlled: a source silently removed here disappears from the coverage denominator.

## Step 2 — Implement the search

The search has two halves that together implement 'record and examine':

1. **Record (completeness):** `tstats` counts audit events per ePHI sourcetype over the review window. Because `tstats` only returns sourcetypes that produced events, a fully-silent source would simply be absent — so the search `append`s the inventory with `audit_events=0` and then `stats max(...) by sourcetype`. The result is one row per *expected* source: a silent source survives as a zero-count row and is labelled `GAP`, which is the failure mode that matters most (a feed that quietly stopped).
2. **Examine (activity review):** the same row carries `audit_events`, `reporting_hosts`, and `last_event`, giving the reviewer the per-source activity volume examined this period.

This `append` + `stats` pattern is used deliberately instead of `join` so no expected source is silently dropped by subsearch truncation. Schedule it on the documented examination cadence (monthly is typical for an access/audit-control review):

```ini
[UC-22.10.59: Audit Controls — ePHI Audit-Log Source Coverage & Periodic Activity Review]
cron_schedule = 0 6 1 * *
dispatch.earliest_time = -30d
dispatch.latest_time = now
actions = summary_index
action.summary_index._name = audit_evidence
action.summary_index.marker = uc=22.10.59,reg=HIPAA_Security,clause=164.312(b)
```

## Step 3 — Validate deployment

**(a) Inventory sanity:** confirm the lookup loads and has the expected row count:

```spl
| inputlookup ephi_audit_sources.csv
| stats count as inventory_sources, dc(sourcetype) as distinct_sourcetypes
```

**(b) Coverage dry-run:** run the base search and confirm every inventory source appears exactly once and that recording sources show non-zero `audit_events`.

**(c) Negative test:** with all feeds healthy, confirm zero GAP rows (see controlTest negativeScenario).

**(d) Positive test:** pause one feed for the window and confirm it surfaces as a GAP row (see controlTest positiveScenario).

## Step 4 — Operationalize (dashboard and reporting)

Build the dashboard 'Audit controls — ePHI source coverage':

**Panel 1 — Single value:** '% of in-scope ePHI sources recording' = recording / inventory total. This is the headline audit-control health number.

**Panel 2 — Coverage table:** system, owner, sourcetype, audit_events, last_event, coverage_status — GAP rows highlighted red. This is the record an auditor reads for §164.312(b).

**Panel 3 — Activity trend:** `timechart` of audit_events per source so the examiner can see the activity volume reviewed and spot collapses that stop short of a full GAP.

Enable scheduled PDF export on the examination cadence and archive to the restricted audit_evidence index.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting and HIPAA caveats

• **A source shows GAP but is healthy:** check the sourcetype string in `ephi_audit_sources.csv` matches the live sourcetype exactly (case-sensitive), and that the index is in the search's `where` clause.

• **Retention:** HIPAA requires 6 years of audit log retention. Verify `frozenTimePeriodInSecs >= 189216000` for `epic`, `mssql`, and `windows`, and that the archive tier is provisioned — otherwise the evidence this control produces cannot itself be retained for the required period.

• **Scope discipline:** the control's credibility rests on the inventory. An ePHI system missing from `ephi_audit_sources.csv` is invisible to the coverage check; periodically reconcile the lookup against the Privacy Officer's system-of-record inventory, not against index names alone.
grandmaExplanation: We keep a master list of every system that holds health records and check that each one is still writing down who looked at the records — and we review that activity on a set schedule. If any system quietly stops keeping its log, we spot the gap right away instead of finding out during an audit.
